subject: physics
title: Contact and non-contact forces
key_idea: A force is a push or pull that acts on an object because of another object. Contact forces act when objects touch. Non-contact forces act across a gap. When two objects interact, each feels a force.

blocks.text: Forces come from interactions between objects. Every force is either a contact force or a non-contact force.

items.meaning: A push or pull on an object caused by its interaction with another object.
A force between objects that are physically touching.
A force between objects that are physically separated.

items: Friction
Air resistance
Tension
Normal contact force
Gravitational force, which gives an object its weight
Electrostatic force
Magnetic force
Each acts through a field: gravitational, electrostatic or magnetic.

blocks.text: The normal contact force is the push of a surface on an object resting on it. Force is a vector quantity, so it has size and direction.

diagram.alt: Sort seven forces into contact and non-contact forces.
diagram.prompt: Sort each force into contact or non-contact.

items: Contact forces need the objects to touch.
Non-contact forces act across a gap.
Weight is a non-contact force.

blocks.text: Each force is linked to a situation you can recall in an exam.

rows: Keeps the Earth in orbit around the Sun
Moves small pieces of paper towards a plastic comb
A magnet pulls on a magnetic material across a gap
Opposes the motion between two surfaces, such as a wheel and an axle
Acts on a falling ball; a smaller area means less air resistance
The table pushes up on a mug resting on it

items: Friction opposes motion between surfaces in contact.
More friction makes it harder to push or turn something.
Air resistance depends on the area of the object.

blocks.text: A force always involves two objects. Each object feels a force from the other, so forces arise in pairs.

items: A mug on a table: the mug pushes down on the table, and the table pushes up on the mug.
A person on bathroom scales: the downward force on the scales is the same size as the upward force on the person.
Each force in a pair can be drawn as a vector, an arrow with a size and a direction.

blocks.text: A stationary rocket on the ground has two forces on it: an upward normal contact force and a downward weight. These act on the same object, so they are not an interaction pair.

items: Forces arise when two objects interact.
The two forces in a pair act on different objects.
The two forces in a pair are the same size.

checks.q: State what is meant by a contact force and a non-contact force. Give one example of each.
checks.a: A contact force acts between objects that are touching, for example friction. A non-contact force acts between objects that are separated, for example gravitational, electrostatic or magnetic force.

checks.q: A mug is placed on a table. Describe the two forces in the interaction pair.
checks.a: The force of the mug on the table. The force of the table on the mug.

checks.q: Name the upward force and the downward force on a rocket that is stationary on the ground.
checks.a: The upward force is the normal contact force. The downward force is weight.

worked_example.question: Two table tennis balls are different sizes but have the same mass. Both balls were dropped onto the table from the same height. After they were dropped, the resultant force on the smaller ball was greater than the resultant force on the larger ball. Explain why.
answer_points: The smaller ball has a smaller area.
So the air resistance is less on the smaller ball.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the smaller area, one for less air resistance on the smaller ball.

worked_example.question: A worker uses a wheelbarrow to move some sand. Some sand falls down and sticks between the wheel and the axle. State why it might be harder to push the wheelbarrow along when there is some sand between the wheel and the axle.
answer_points: There will be more friction between the axle and the wheel.
worked_example.tip: Name the force: friction. Say where it acts, between the axle and the wheel.

worked_example.question: A builder places a mug on a table. Describe the two forces in the interaction pair when the mug is placed on the table.
answer_points: The force of the mug on the table (gravity or the force due to gravity is allowed).
The force of the table on the mug (normal contact force is allowed).
worked_example.tip: Name both objects in each force and say which acts on which.

blocks.text: This section covers what friction does between two solid surfaces.

items: Solid friction is the force between two surfaces that may impede motion.
Friction between rubbing surfaces also produces heating.

worked_example.question: A puck travels across some rough ice. The rough ice exerts a frictional force on the puck. Explain how the force of friction changes the velocity of the puck.
answer_points: The velocity (speed) of the puck decreases.
The force of friction acts in the opposite direction to the velocity.
worked_example.tip: Say that the force is opposite to the motion. Slows down or decelerates is accepted.

blocks.text: A force can change the speed, shape or direction of an object.

items: Speed: a driving force makes a car speed up, and friction from the brakes slows it down.
Shape: squeezing a sponge or stretching a spring changes its shape.
Direction: a kick from the side changes the direction of a rolling ball.
